strategies.name: Naive Sequential All-Reduce Loop
strategies.desc: Directly follows the reference implementation with 8 sequential all-reduce calls, each preceded by bidiagonal coupling and followed by inverse coupling. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces (plus initial). Represents the baseline: simplest structure, maximum latency from sequential collective synchronization, no optimization for communication-computation overlap.

strategies.name: Pipelined Ring All-Reduce Custom
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a manual ring implementation (reduce-scatter + all-gather pattern) to pipeline the 8 stages, overlapping communication of stage i with local computation (coupling/uncoupling) of stage i+1. Dispatch count: ~16 (2 per stage for RS+AG). Trades primitive simplicity for potential latency hiding through fine-grained asynchronous dispatch.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc: Exploit 224 = 28 nodes × 8 devices structure by first performing intra-node reductions (8-way), then inter-node reductions (28-way), applying bidiagonal coupling at the appropriate hierarchy level. Dispatch count: ~16 all-reduces (8 stages × 2 levels). Reduces cross-node bandwidth pressure by factoring communication topology, at cost of added local aggregation overhead.

strategies.name: Fused Coupling with Reduce-Scatter/All-Gather
strategies.desc: Decompose each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, fusing the bidiagonal coupling into the reduce-scatter output buffer and inverse coupling into all-gather input buffer to eliminate intermediate full-size tensor materialization. Dispatch count: 16 collectives (RS+AG per stage). Reduces memory footprint and bandwidth by operating on W×smaller shards during coupling operations.

strategies.name: Batched All-Reduce with Delayed Coupling
strategies.desc:
Group multiple stages' all-reduce operations into a single batched collective call (concatenating buffers), then apply all coupling/uncoupling transformations on the batched result in one fused kernel. Dispatch count: 2-4 large all-reduces instead of 8. Minimizes dispatch overhead and synchronization barriers at the cost of larger per-message payload and reduced ability to overlap computation with communication.
